caveats: Only Lectures 1-8 of 19 are covered; the KB cannot answer questions about the technical content of Lectures 9-19.
Lecture 1's recording leaves out the course-logistics slides (5-6 and 10-15); their content comes from the slides alone.
Lecture 2's recording ends after slide 21; slides 22-27 (collecting demonstrations, the embodiment gap, the summary) come from the slides alone.
Lecture 3's recording does not discuss slide 2's reminders and skips the KL constraint on slide 25 for time; that constraint comes from the slides alone.

Lecture 4's recording ends on the review slide (23); its slides 24-37 (off-policy actor-critic, replay buffers, soft actor-critic, the SAC-versus-PPO chart, the closing slides) are not discussed in that recording, but Lecture 5 teaches the same material aloud from a revised deck.

Lecture 5's recording covers slides 3-28; slide 2's reminders and slides 29-30 (plan recap, next time) come from the slides alone. Several steps (a KL-penalized objective, the clipping written out, the recursive Q-function) were worked on a board the recording does not show and are reconstructed from the spoken words.

Lecture 6's recording covers slides 3-29; slide 2's reminders and slide 29's next-week topics come from the slides alone. Slide 7's thought exercise is answered while pointing at the slide, and the algorithm is written on a board the recording does not show; the wiki reconstructs both from the spoken words and says so. Slides 24-25 print the n-step target's discount exponent as t - t', which the wiki notes as an apparent slip.

Lecture 7's recording covers slides 3-23 and 30-32. It does not teach the conservative-methods section (slides 24-28, conservative Q-learning) or slide 31's LinkedIn application, which Lecture 8 teaches aloud from the same slides, and it does not discuss slides 2 and 33. Much of the lecture is written or drawn live; the wiki reconstructs that work from the spoken words and says so. Slides 4, 18 and 19 print the Monte Carlo target's reward at t inside a sum over t', which the wiki notes as an apparent slip. In its worked advantage example the returns as captioned (+10, +1, -5) average to 2, not the 3 the lecturer uses; the wiki says so.

Lecture 8's recording covers slides 3-32; slides 2 and 34 (reminders, the guest-lecture announcement) and slide 33 come from the slides alone. Its CQL derivation and goal-classifier picture are worked on a board the recording does not show, the CQL objective in the critic's parameters rather than the slides' notation; the wiki reconstructs both from the spoken words and says so. In the recap's worked example the Q-value of the first action is written on the board and never read out. Slide 29 prints the RLHF stage's sub-line as the supervised stage's, which the wiki notes as an apparent copy slip.

Transcripts are copy-edited from YouTube auto-captions; students are inaudible, so their questions appear only as the lecturer restates them. Lectures 1 and 2 each have three passages marked [Ed: unclear], Lecture 3 one, Lecture 4 two, Lecture 5 five (plus four flagged restorations). Lecture 6's captions are much noisier: 53 of its 80 paragraphs carry [Ed:] notes, mostly on garbled board dictation and mis-heard notation. Lecture 7's captions are cleaner: 8 [Ed:] notes in 7 of its 88 paragraphs. Lecture 8 has 4 [Ed:] notes in its 86 paragraphs.
The verbatim captions are not committed; each transcript says how to regenerate them.
